newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Briefing - Apr14.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Briefing - Apr14.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from the German press and from Reuters on Advertising, Marketing, Brand-name Products, Consumer Trends, Media and the Internet
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - German automaker Seat Deutschland GmbH beat back industry rumours about a shift in its advertising representation by signing a long-term contract with Wilkens GmbH as its lead German ad agency, Wilkens says. (Reuter)
BONN - The 1996 sponsoring concept for T-Mobil cellular telephone rates Telly D1 has won the fifth German sponsoring prize, says the German communications association. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - CKS Holding Central Europe has opened in Hamburg as a new agency for integrated marketing and new media. The holding is comprised of CKS Partners, new media specialist CKS Digital World and the service and distribution company CKS Realtime.
(Horizont)

DUESSELDORF - The Duesseldorf advertising agency Grey says it has started its launch campaign for the Skoda mid-market model Octavia. The agency says it plans a campaign for television, newspapers and magazines. (Reuter)
COLOGNE - The Cologne advertising agency Barten & Barten says it has introduced three new cinema ads with entertainer Dirk Bach for the newspaper "Express." (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Television ratings researcher A.C. Nielsen's German unit has called for charges to be brought against a former employee of the company, news magazine Focus reports. The magazine says the company accuses a former managing director of giving preferential treatment to his son in distributing Nielsen projects. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BERLIN - Public television network ARD's chairman Udo Reiter would like to move one of the station's headquarters to Berlin by the year 2000, reports the Berlin daily newspaper Tagesspiegel. ARD-Berlin would be operated by the Berlin state government and six other state broadcasting authorities.
(Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Pierre Dauzier, director of the French media company Havas S.A., Paris, has announced a change in share holdings in CLT-Ufa. The French shareholders own 10 percent of the company, which Dauzier said was insufficient. "Either we increase our share and become a significant stockholder or we will sell," says Dauzier. (Handelsblatt)

FRANKFURT - A fight over private television station Kabel 1's use of the number one in its logo, the Cologne regional appellate court has ruled partly in favour of public broadcaster ARD, which also uses a number one in its logo, in its suit. The court's verdict prohibits Kabel 1 from using the logo in audiovisual material or in advertising. (Horizont)

HAMBURG - For the first time, a German court has found a television producer guilty of falsifying ratings. The Munich district court has ruled that Joerg Hoffmeister, former general director of broadcaster NDR-Funkhaus Hanover and executive producer of Tele-FAZ, systematically rounded up the ratings of a medical news programme on all-news network n-tv from April 1995 until the end of that year. (Der Spiegel)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

HANOVER - Chancellor Helmut Kohl has opened the 50th Hanover industrial fair, which organisers say presents booths from 7,259 companies from 69 countries. Britain is the 1997 fair's "partner country". (Reuter)

MUNICH - German industrial group Thyssen AG will decide in the next three months whether to sell its 30 percent share of the E-Plus mobile phone network, its chief exeuctive says. "We have the option to leave it purely mobile, develop an integrated telecommunications provider out of E-Plus or to sell our share," Dieter Vogel tells the newsweekly Focus. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
FRANKFURT - Burkhard Breiing has taken over as director of business marketing for Citibank Privatkunden AG of Duesseldorf.
(Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Luxury auto maker BMW has reorganised its German distribution leadership for foreign markets. Ralph Weyler has taken over as director of the new distribution group. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - The MundoSales unit of advertising agency Publicis says has tapped Jutta Fischer as account executive for German Renault AG, says Publicis. She will be responsible for trade marketing, says the Publicis Werbeagentur GmbH. (Reuter)
